headline: I Filed An RTI Request To Know Which Files Are Exempt From The RTI Act, And Now My Mailbox Just Emits A Low-Frequency Hum
body:
I thought I was being clever last Tuesday. As a concerned citizen with a penchant for bureaucracy, I filed a request under the Right to Information Act simply asking for a list of all documents currently classified under the newly exempted 'Public (Law and Order) Department.' I expected a delayed response, or perhaps a form letter explaining the legal nuance of the exemption. Instead, I received a thick, beige envelope delivered by a man in a vest who refused to make eye contact.

Inside, there was no list. There was only a single, perfectly blank sheet of paper and a small, battery-operated buzzer taped to the center. When I touched the paper, the buzzer activated, emitting a sound that the manual—which appeared in my mailbox an hour later—identifies as 'The Sound of Absolute Privacy.'

Since then, my neighbors have complained that my home emits a constant, low-frequency thrum that makes their milk curdle. I tried to walk to the local post office to inquire about the status of my inquiry, but every time I mention the words 'Right to Information,' a small cloud of localized static follows me for three blocks. I am starting to think that by asking what is hidden, I have inadvertently become a piece of classified government infrastructure myself.

I reached out to a legal friend, but he advised me to stop talking entirely, noting that if I keep pushing, I might be upgraded to a 'Top Secret Filing Cabinet' and permanently relocated to a basement in Chennai. For now, I have decided to embrace the hum. It’s actually quite soothing, provided you don't try to read anything or ask any follow-up questions.
caption: When the government says 'no,' they really mean 'we are turning your house into a hum-based signal tower.' My RTI journey has officially entered the void. #BureaucracyLife #RTI #TransparencyGoneWild #Satire (satire)
igHook: Have you ever accidentally filed a request that ended up with the government turning your home into a piece of classified infrastructure?

It avoids the AI tendency to wink at the joke, maintaining a perfect, deadpan tone that treats the bureaucratic absurdity as a genuine life crisis.
